overnightRisk: Five specific things can move this market before the 02:00 COT report, and for the first time in a week the biggest one is not crypto-native. ONE - NVIDIA. Results landed after the US close: 96.2bn USD revenue, up 106 percent year on year, 2.22 EPS against 1.05, 75.0 percent gross margin, and Jensen Huang guiding to 70 percent fiscal-2028 revenue growth with supply secured. QQQ is 719.77 after hours, up 1.18 percent. BTC has tracked the Nasdaq closely through August and the Asian session will price this print in full. The asymmetry is real but it cuts both ways: a beat this large is now IN the after-hours price, so the overnight risk is a fade of the initial pop rather than the print itself. TWO - the PCE inflation reading came in hot the same session, and the 10-year at 4.65 percent has already given back 1.4 basis points. If Asia decides hot PCE outweighs the NVDA beat, the after-hours risk-on unwinds and BTC gives back the 425.7 points it gained since midday. THREE - the ETF tape is INCOMPLETE. Farside's 26 August row shows FBTC +25.6m, BITB +6.0m, MSBT +3.4m, BTC +46.8m and GBTC -50.4m for a partial total of +31.4m, with IBIT and BRRR still showing dashes. IBIT supplied 284.4m of the 314.3m total on 25 August. If IBIT completes near zero or negative, the seven-session inflow streak breaks on a day the desk just added, and it will break after this report is published. FOUR - the corridor is EMPTY. Both liquidation ladders were spent today: 4.46m USD of longs executed at 78,000 to 77,500 this morning, 6.44m of shorts at 78,500 to 79,250 this afternoon. There is no cushion of resting fuel between 78,200 and 79,250 to slow a directional move, which in an overnight session with thin books means a push either way travels further than it should. FIVE - the retail long/short account ratio at 1.13 is the highest of the day and it re-crowded INTO the bounce, so the marginal overnight long is a late one. That combination - crowded latecomers above an empty corridor - is precisely the setup that produced this morning's 869-point flush, which is why the resting stop below is recommended rather than optional.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull moves to BALANCED, and that is a change of state rather than a hedge. Midday called it UP on the argument that the downside fuel had been spent while the short fuel above was intact and untouched. The first half of that held and the second half was consumed within four hours: the rally to 79,172.6 executed roughly 6.44m USD of shorts across 78,500 through 79,250, with the top two rungs printing 100 percent short. The 24h ledger now reads 5,947,844 USD long against 5,674,639 short, a ratio of 1.05 to 1, against 3.88 to 1 at midday and 3.12 to 1 at morning. Both ladders are receipts. There is no dense unspent pool in either direction between 78,200 and 79,250, and the honest consequence is that the next directional move has less to lean on and less to slow it down - which matters more overnight than it does intraday. Corroborating detail, and it is the one bullish item in this paragraph: open interest is 2,302,375,311 USD, UP 0.91 percent from midday's 2,281,704,862 and the first rise in three sessions. Because 6.44m of shorts were force-closed during that same window - which mechanically REDUCES open interest - a net increase means new positions were opened faster than old ones were closed. That is participation, not covering. The counterweights are two. Funding is 0.0000520157 per 8h, down from midday's 0.0000662 and effectively neutral, and the perp premium is still NEGATIVE at -0.0003753, so the perp is trading below the index even after a 1,557-point round trip - there is no leverage euphoria financing this. But the long/short account ratio has climbed 1.08 at midday to 1.10 at 21:00Z to 1.14 at 22:00Z to 1.13 at 00:00Z, its high of the day. Retail cut net-long exposure INTO this morning's low and has re-crowded long INTO the recovery, which is the wrong order. Crowded latecomers sitting above an empty corridor is the specific reason the overnight stop is recommended.
